text:
carmen: Heads-up: OraclePartner dropped a daily usage export and the consumption hierarchy (sku -> plan -> bundle) isn't represented. Their CSV uses `sku_code` only and some SKUs are actually add-ons that should map to a parent plan. We need mapping rules and a safe ingest fallback.
tobias: can you paste a sample row?
carmen: sample (sanitized):
```
sku_code,reported_ts,qty,unit,partner_batch_id
OP-DB-SIZE,2026-03-24T05:00:00Z,2048,megabytes,BATCH-OP-20260324-01
OP-BACKUP,2026-03-24T05:00:00Z,1,backup_job,BATCH-OP-20260324-01
```
naveen: OP-BACKUP is an add-on that should be billed under the parent plan OP-DB. If we naively map sku->plan by sku name we'll split revenue. Need a canonical mapping table per partner and a priority rule: parent mapping > sku-level mapping > heuristic.
rachel: also note some partners report both bundle-level SKUs (OP-DB-BUNDLE) and component SKUs in the same batch. We should prefer the bundle SKU for billing and ignore component SKUs when a bundle is present for the same resource id.
oracle-partner-pm: we can provide a mapping manifest that lists sku -> plan_id and group_id (bundle id). ETA tomorrow. We can also emit `resource_id` in next export to correlate components to bundles.
carmen: ingestion heuristics proposal:
- require partner mapping manifest (signed) for any partner with bundles; until manifest arrives, apply conservative rules:
  1) if batch contains a bundle SKU for resource_id X, drop component SKUs for X (tag as "bundle-superseded")
  2) if only component SKUs present, aggregate to parent_plan using manifest if available else use heuristic (prefix match + partner_hint) and tag as "heuristic-mapped"
  3) store original rows and mapping decision for audit
- dedupe key: prefer `external_event_id`; fallback: partner_id + partner_batch_id + sku_code + resource_id + ts_minute
- backfill window: 7 days; require signed manifest for reclassification after initial ingest
pseudocode:
```
if bundle_present(resource_id, batch):
  drop(component_rows for resource_id) and tag 'bundle-superseded'
else if mapping_manifest contains sku:
  map sku -> plan_id
else:
  map heuristically and tag 'heuristic-mapped'
```
billng-bot: alert: oraclepartner-ingest job 2026-03-24T06:12Z -> 1.2k rows processed, 87 heuristic-mapped, 23 bundle-superseded. ticket #4678 opened.
tobias: billing note: for heuristic-mapped items we'll hold the affected line items in "pending" for 48h. If partner manifest later reclassifies to a bundle, we must retroactively adjust invoice lines and reverse charges. Need a clear rollback/rebill playbook.
naveen: operationally, add a reclassification index: keep mapping decisions in a table keyed by (partner_batch_id, resource_id) so we can run idempotent reclassify jobs when manifests arrive. Also require manifest signature and manifest_checksum for acceptance.
rachel: UX: surface "heuristic-mapped" rows in the Partner Reconciliation UI with suggested mapping and a one-click "accept partner mapping" that triggers a reclassify. Also show revenue delta before/after.
oracle-partner-pm: we'll add `resource_id` and produce a mapping manifest today. For older historical batches we can provide a one-off reclassify manifest if needed.
billing-bot: alert: follow-up ticket #4679 created to track reclassification tooling.
carmen: action items:
- oracle-partner-pm: deliver mapping manifest + resource_id in exports (ETA 24h)
- naveen: implement reclassification index + idempotent reclassify job (EOD)
- rachel: UX stub for reconciliation UI to show heuristic rows and accept partner mappings (next sprint)
- tobias: draft rollback/rebill playbook for partner-initiated reclassifications (tomorrow)
carmen: thanks everyone. Once manifest arrives we'll run the reclassify dry-run and post results here. :white_check_mark:
